findings.description: The new G13 assertion `[ ! -e "$TEMP_DIR/tertiary-review.json" ] && [ ! -e "$TEMP_DIR/tertiary-skeptic.json" ]` is a two-operand && list that is followed by further commands in the same @test body. Bash (and therefore bats, which relies on `set -eET` plus an ERR trap) does not fire errexit or the ERR trap for any command in a && list except the one after the final &&. If tertiary-review.json EXISTS, the first test returns 1, the list short-circuits, no trap fires, and the next line (`! grep -q gemini-headless ...`) resets $?. The test passes. Only the tertiary-skeptic.json half of the check can ever fail the test. The comment states the intent is 'no tertiary artefact', so half of that pin is a no-op. (The hunk is labeled .claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh in the diff header but the content is the Flatline tertiary opt-in bats suite; see DISS-002.)
findings.failure_mode: If run_phase1 regresses and writes tertiary-review.json for a tertiary that is disabled_by_opt_in (e.g. an empty or error artefact that downstream consensus later reads as a voice), this test stays green. The review-round fix it was added to pin (r251-1 G13) is only verified for the skeptic artefact.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the check a single command or two separate statements so the ERR trap sees each failure, e.g. `[[ ! -e "$TEMP_DIR/tertiary-review.json" && ! -e "$TEMP_DIR/tertiary-skeptic.json" ]]` or two lines: `[ ! -e "$TEMP_DIR/tertiary-review.json" ]` then `[ ! -e "$TEMP_DIR/tertiary-skeptic.json" ]`. Optionally add an `|| { ls "$TEMP_DIR"; return 1; }` diagnostic like the loop above it. Grep the three touched bats files for other mid-body `] && [` lists.

findings.description: The diff header names `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh` (mode 100755) but both hunks are bats test code: the hunk-context function `_cfg() {  # <tertiary> [agy_opt_in value|absent] [headless mode]`, `$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR`, `run --separate-stderr run_phase1 ...`, `run tertiary_opt_in_skip_reason`, `get_model_tertiary`/`get_tertiary_status` assertions and `local f` with `return 1` are the Flatline tertiary opt-in suite (tests/unit/flatline-tertiary-agy-opt-in.bats per the sprint report). The pre-existing context lines are already bats syntax, so this is almost certainly a mislabeled path in the diff rather than bats code being inserted into the sourced dissent script. It still needs confirming: if these lines really were applied to adversarial-review.sh, sourcing it would execute test assertions at load time and fail.
findings.failure_mode: If the hunks were genuinely applied to .claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh, the dissent script would run bats-only constructs (`run --separate-stderr`, top-level `return 1`, `[ "$status" -eq 0 ]`) when sourced or executed and break every /review dissent invocation. If the path is merely mislabeled, the only consequence is that findings anchored to it (including DISS-001) point at the wrong file.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm with `git show --stat` that the hunks landed in tests/unit/flatline-tertiary-agy-opt-in.bats and that .claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh is unchanged in this commit; regenerate the diff if the header was rewritten by tooling. If the file is genuinely adversarial-review.sh, revert the two hunks and move them to the bats suite.
